item.title: Lunar soil reads as a cosmic time capsule for exploding stars
item.description: When a star reaches its final stages of life, it ends in a bright, powerful explosion called a supernova and scatters material across the universe. A new study led by a University of Hawai'i at Mānoa researcher has discovered that the moon's mixed-up soil can be read as a cosmic time capsule for exploding stars. The work is published in the journal Physical Review Letters. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: 9,000-year-old arrowheads covered in strange markings leave archaeologists puzzled
item.description: Unearthed from the depths of Turkey, ancient arrowheads reveal enigmatic hand-carved symbols. These Neolithic treasures showcase intentional incisions rather than random scratches, prompting researchers to ponder their origins. Despite thorough investigations, the specific purpose behind these markings remains unknown. Observations indicate that this intriguing practice was limited to select communities, leaving archaeologists grappling with unanswered questions about their significance. item.title: A 'super El Niño' could make India's monsoon drier yet more dangerous
item.description: India is currently in the middle of its summer monsoon, but this year's rainfall presents an interesting paradox. Much of the country has received less rain than usual so far, yet has still been hit by severe floods and landslides. In the southern state of Kerala, for example, devastating floods occurred despite the overall monsoon rainfall remaining well below average. Fuente: Phys.org.
